item.title: WAF restores water supply to CWM Hospital after shortage leaves patients relying on bottled water
item.description: CWM Hospital patients were affected by a water shortage after the hospital’s backup water tank ran dry following a burst water pipe, leaving critical services disrupted and patients relying on bottled water. Water supply has since been restored following flushing operations by the Water Authority of Fiji.
item.content:encoded:
CWM Hospital patients were affected by a water shortage after the hospital’s backup water tank ran dry following a burst water pipe, leaving critical services disrupted and patients relying on bottled water.

Water supply has since been restored following flushing operations by the Water Authority of Fiji.

Hospital Medical Superintendent Dr Luke Nasedra has confirmed with fijivillage News that the hospital had been without a proper running water supply since yesterday.

He says the shortage slowed services in the Intensive Care Unit, Acute Medical Ward, Operating Theatre and Emergency Department.

Despite the challenges, Dr Nasedra confirms that the Emergency Department remained operational during the disruption.

He says the hospital had been working closely with WAF to restore the water supply as soon as possible.

International Women's Association President Judy Compain has raised concerns about the impact of the water shortage on patients, questioning why the situation at the hospital had not received greater attention from political leaders.

Compain says the Intensive Care Unit, Operating Theatre and Emergency Department in the hospital’s East Wing were at risk because of the lack of water.

She questions what would happen if emergency surgery was needed while the hospital was without water.

Compain says politicians should focus their time and energy on the crisis affecting patients and hold each other accountable for the state of the country’s health facilities.

She also questions why political leaders had not issued statements about the situation at the hospital, asking whether the issue only mattered when someone they knew or cared about was affected.

WAF confirms that water supply has been restored, adding that repairs to a burst water main on Belo Street, scheduled for tonight, may result in further water pressure fluctuations.

The Authority says the hospital’s water tanks will refill as supply is restored.

item.title: Emergency water deliveries continue in martime areas as families in Yasawa and Cikobia face shortages
item.description: Families facing water shortages in the Yasawa Group and Cikobia will continue to receive emergency water supplies as authorities work to assist affected communities in the maritime areas. The National Disaster Risk Management Office says water deliveries, which began last week, will continue in both maritime areas.
item.content:encoded:
Families facing water shortages in the Yasawa Group and Cikobia will continue to receive emergency water supplies as authorities work to assist affected communities in the maritime areas.

The National Disaster Risk Management Office says water deliveries, which began last week, will continue in both maritime areas.

In the Western Division, the MLC Vunilagi will continue delivering water to affected communities in the Yasawa Group, while the vessel MLC Vatulawa will continue delivering emergency water supplies to residents in Cikobia in the Northern Division.

The NDRMO says the operations are being carried out in collaboration with the Ministry of Public Works, Meteorological Services and Transport, the Water Authority of Fiji and other agencies.

They say water deliveries will continue based on the needs of affected communities and weather conditions.

Residents are also urged to conserve water and use their available supplies wisely.

The NDRMO says it will continue monitoring the situation and providing further updates.
